beats.intro: Module thirteen. [[sub]]Risk measures for bonds with uncertain cash flows, and for changes in the shape of the yield curve.
beats.effective: Yield duration assumes cash flows are certain. [[opt]]A callable bond breaks that. If rates fall, it may be called early, so there is no single yield to maturity. [[ed]]The right measure is effective duration: how much the price changes when the benchmark yield curve shifts in parallel. [[f]]Effective duration is the price after a downward shift, minus the price after an upward shift, divided by twice the shift, times the original price. [[ec]]Effective convexity adds the two shifted prices, subtracts twice the original, and divides by the shift squared, times the original price. [[mod]]The shifted prices come from an option pricing model. It uses the call schedule, credit spreads, and an assumption about interest rate volatility. [[ex]]For the five year bond, shifted prices of one hundred point two four one, and ninety nine point seven six, give an effective duration of four point eight one.
beats.callable: Compare a callable bond with an otherwise identical non-callable bond. [[nc]]The non-callable price rises steadily as the benchmark yield falls. [[c]]The callable price is always lower. The difference is the value of the call option, held by the issuer. [[hi]]When yields are high, the option is worth little, and the two bonds behave alike. [[lo]]When yields are low, the issuer is likely to call, and the callable bond's price stops rising. [[neg]]Its slope flattens, so its effective duration falls, and its effective convexity turns negative. [[put]]A putable bond is the mirror image. The put protects the investor when yields rise, so duration falls when rates rise. [[mbs]]Mortgage-backed securities behave like callable bonds, because homeowners refinance when rates fall.
beats.est: With effective duration and convexity, we can estimate the price change for a parallel shift. [[f]]Minus effective duration times the shift, plus half the effective convexity times the shift squared. [[ex]]Take a callable bond with effective duration six point oh nine four, and effective convexity of minus two hundred thirty. The benchmark curve rises fifty basis points. [[dur]]The duration effect is minus three point oh four seven percent. [[cvx]]The negative convexity subtracts another point two eight eight. [[tot]]The total is minus three point three three percent. [[note]]For a callable bond, the convexity term hurts in both directions.
beats.keyrate: Effective duration assumes the whole curve moves together. Key rate duration measures sensitivity to one maturity at a time. [[def]]Shift only the two year rate, then only the five year, then only the ten year, and measure each price change. [[sum]]The key rate durations add up to the effective duration. [[ex]]Take a portfolio of two, five, and ten year government bonds, with equal par. Its duration is five point three four five. [[bars]]The key rate durations are zero point six seven six at two years, one point six three two at five years, and three point oh three seven at ten years. [[sc]]Suppose only the two year rate rises twenty five basis points, flattening the curve. The price falls by about point one seven percent. [[use]]Managers use key rate durations to tilt a portfolio toward the curve changes they expect, and to see shaping risk.
beats.empirical: So far, durations are analytical. They use formulas, and assume benchmark yields and credit spreads move independently. [[emp]]Empirical duration instead uses historical data and statistical models. [[ex]]In a crisis, investors flee to government bonds. [[gov]]Benchmark yields fall, which raises prices. [[spr]]But credit spreads widen, which lowers the prices of risky bonds. [[net]]The net gain is smaller than analytical duration predicts. So empirical duration is lower for such bonds. [[use]]For government bonds, the two measures are similar. For a corporate portfolio, especially high yield, empirical duration is more relevant.
beats.wrap: Let's recap. [[w1]]Effective duration and convexity handle embedded options. [[w2]]Callable bonds have lower duration, and negative convexity, when yields fall. [[w3]]Key rate durations measure the risk of curve shape changes, and sum to effective duration. [[w4]]Empirical duration reflects the correlation between yields and credit spreads.
